sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: retake waits, license ages, curfews, validity periods, phone rules, CDL limits and photo exemptions
Confusable pairs among the licensing and probationary rules, followed by continuation facts the main list did not hold; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
A failed skills exam means a seven-day wait, but a third failure while still on a permit means a two-month wait from the latest failed attempt. [A01]
Why it matters: group skills exam; confusable ordinary retake versus third failure.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A03
With a completed BMV licensed driver education program the license age is 16, while without one it is 16 years and 270 days. [A03]
Why it matters: group license age; confusable with versus without driver education.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A04
During the first one hundred eighty days, probationary drivers cannot drive from ten p.m. to five a.m.; afterward while under eighteen, driving is barred after eleven p.m. Sunday through Thursday, before five a.m. Monday through Friday, and from one a.m. to five a.m. Saturday and Sunday unless traveling for lawful work, a school-sanctioned activity, or a religious event, or riding with a qualifying licensed adult twenty-five or older or licensed spouse twenty-one or older [A04].
Why it matters: group probationary hours; confusable first period versus later period.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A04
A probationary license is valid until 21 years and 30 days, but it can be renewed only from 21 years and one day. [A04]
Why it matters: group probationary validity; confusable expiry versus earliest renewal.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A03
Drivers under 75 get six-year licenses, those aged 75 through 84 get three-year licenses and those 85 or older get two-year licenses. [A03]
Why it matters: group validity; confusable age bands.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A03
A CDL lasts four years, and licenses for lawful temporary residents may not follow the standard validity periods. [A03]
Why it matters: group validity; confusable CDL versus regular license.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A05
Probationary license holders are barred from using any telecommunications device while driving except to place a nine-one-one emergency call, whereas the general rule for all drivers bars typing, sending, or reading texts or emails while driving unless using hands-free or voice-operated technology or calling nine-one-one [A05] [A05].
Why it matters: group phones; confusable probationary versus all-driver rule.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A03
A disabled applicant aged 16 or 17 needs the 180-day permit hold and a practice log, but one aged 18 or older needs neither. [A03]
Why it matters: group disability; confusable under versus over eighteen.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A01
Reversing skills, including backing correctly out of a parking space, are part of what the examiner scores. [A01]
Why it matters: group skills exam; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A01
Slowing down while changing lanes, reversing too fast, leaving the signal on after finishing a lane change and following or passing parked vehicles too closely can also cost points. [A01]
Why it matters: group skills exam; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A01
Even after a driver has failed the skills exam, the BMV examiner may choose to let the drive continue. [A01]
Why it matters: group skills exam; misconception exam stops at failure.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A02
If financial liability is canceled, the minor must apply for an amended learner's permit with a different adult signing for financial liability. [A02]
Why it matters: group financial liability; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A05
An Indiana CDL covers vehicles or combinations rated over 26,000 pounds, vehicles built or used to carry 16 or more people including the driver, and hazardous material vehicles with the right class and endorsement. [A05]
Why it matters: group commercial; scope note CDL only.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A05
Photo-exempt permits and licenses are offered for medical or religious reasons, photo-exempt ID cards only for religious reasons, and the BMV still takes a photo to keep on file. [A05]
Why it matters: group credentials; confusable medical versus religious exemption.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A05
A credential will not reach you if your postal address change was not also given to the BMV, which accepts updates at a branch, online or at a BMV Connect kiosk. [A05]
Why it matters: group credentials; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A06
The legal definition of a telecommunications device covers phones, PDAs, pagers and texting devices but leaves out licensed CB radio use and communications systems in commercial vehicles weighing more than 10,000 pounds. [A06]
Why it matters: group phones; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A06
Using a telecommunications device while driving can put points on your driver record. [A06]
Why it matters: group phones; link to points chapter.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0017]
